newsitem.title: UK: Analysts seen shaving M&G profit forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Analysts seen shaving M&G profit forecasts.

text.p: Analysts said on Thursday they expected a downgrading of full-year profit forecasts for fund manager M&G Group Plc following disappointing half-year earnings.
M&G said earlier half-year, pre-tax profits came in six percent higher at 33.2 million sterling from 31.2 million a year earlier, while the interim dividend was maintained at 16 pence.
Costs related to windfall personal equity plans (PEPs) and a charge for readying systems for the millennium date change were likely to depress second half-figures.
"(Windfall PEPs) are certainly not going to make them a profit in the second half," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
M&G said the cost of preparing its systems for the date change at the end of the century was likely to come in at five million sterling over 18 months.
Some non-recurring costs related to relaunching its UK equity unit trust products later in the year were also likely to come through, he said.

"It is not all doom and gloom in the sense that some of the downgrade will relate to them quantifying the cost of the millennium project and they have also indicated the timing in the second half of the reorganising of their unit trust stable," said UBS analyst Martin Cross.

But revenues, initial charges and annual fees were running lower than expected. He said he would be cutting the full-year, pre-tax forecast to about 68 million sterling from 76 million and didn't see dividend growth above single digits.
First-half earnings growth was hit by its underperforming UK unit trust business, and the group said it was looking to refocus the product and improve the investment process.

The analyst who asked not to be named said longer term prospects for the group were more positive and it was well placed in its institutional business. But it did need to get its UK equity unit trust business back on track.
He expected full-year, pre-tax profits to be up on last year at nearly 75 million sterling, and a small increase in the final dividend.

M&G's share price fell sharply on the profit announcement, trading 61.5 pence lower at 12.84 stg by 1200 GMT. The analyst said the share price fall was probably overdone, but the stock had run a strong run recently.

Cross said several factors were pointing in the right direction for the group, including outperformance of some higher yielding indices, some funds moving into the second or top quartile in terms of performance and a strong pension fund showing.

While the group would face a difficult 12 months, it was supported by the historical trend of value investing coming good over time, and it was likely to have the backup of finding an investor in the shares if it didn't, he said.
M&G could look to a merger with a large financial institution with a relatively tame customer base but that was unlikely to come up for at least a year or two.
